speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; can you tell me how long the bleeding has lasted and if you have noticed any other bruising on your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the family history of joint swelling alongside bleeding is concerning. Given the severity of the gum bleeding, can you describe any spontaneous bleeding elsewhere, such as nosebleeds or blood in your urine, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, aPTT, Platelet Count).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The results show a significantly prolonged aPTT (60 sec) with normal PT and platelet count, which strongly suggests an intrinsic pathway defect. Given your family history of joint swelling and bleeding, have you ever experienced painful bleeding into your joints, such as your knees or elbows? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of affected joints if patient confirms symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A.

The prolonged aPTT with normal PT and platelet count, combined with your family history of joint swelling and bleeding, is classic for a Factor VIII deficiency. Based on this clinical evidence, I have made my diagnosis.
